questions.q: What does creating a group in Tableau actually do to your data?
options: It creates a new field that combines several existing dimension members into one, without changing the underlying data source
It permanently deletes the original, ungrouped members from the data source
It writes a new table back to the connected database
It merges two different data sources into one
questions.explain: Grouping creates a new field (like Sub-Category (group)) that combines members you choose — it never modifies or deletes anything in the underlying data source.

questions.q: In the Edit Group dialog, what does checking 'Include Other' do?
options: Rolls every remaining, non-grouped member into a single catch-all 'Other' member
Deletes every member that wasn't included in a group
Automatically renames all groups to 'Other'
Hides the group entirely from the view
questions.explain: 'Include Other' buckets everything you didn't explicitly group into one 'Other' member — useful for spotlighting a few groups against everything else.

questions.q: How do you build a hierarchy in the Data pane?
options: Drag one field and drop it directly on top of another field you want it nested under (or right-click and choose Create Hierarchy)
Open the Edit Group dialog and click Group
Type a formula into a calculated field
Hierarchies can only be created automatically by Tableau, never manually
questions.explain: Dragging a field onto another in the Data pane (or right-clicking a field and choosing Create Hierarchy) is how you build a manual hierarchy like Category-to-Sub-Category.

questions.q: What does Tableau automatically build a hierarchy for, without you doing anything?
options: Any date field — it's automatically broken into Year, Quarter, Month, and Day
Every string field in the data source
Only fields named 'Category'
Nothing is ever built automatically; every hierarchy must be created manually
questions.explain: Tableau auto-builds a date hierarchy (Year > Quarter > Month > Day) the moment you connect to data with a date field — that's why date fields already show a drill-down arrow.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a group and a hierarchy?
options: A group manually combines specific members into one new member; a hierarchy nests existing fields so you can drill up and down between them
They are two names for the exact same feature
A hierarchy changes the underlying data source, while a group does not
A group can only be built on date fields, while a hierarchy works on any field
questions.explain: Groups combine specific members into a new member (edit-the-data-view); hierarchies nest existing fields for drill-down/drill-up navigation (navigate-the-data-view). Sets, covered next lesson, add a dynamic in/out condition on top.
